title: Drag slows something moving through a liquid or a gas
summary: Drag is a force that opposes and slows an object moving through a fluid such as air or water.
body: OpenStax Physics says drag opposes and slows the motion of an object through a fluid. On the same page, air resistance is named as a form of friction. The point for everyday motion is that moving through air or water costs speed unless something keeps pushing. The book does not give a drag formula on this page. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020.

sources.title: 4.2 Newton's First Law of Motion: Inertia
sources.author: Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs
sources.note: Paraphrase only, not a quotation. OpenStax Physics, Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs, published 26 March 2020. The assigned licence for /books/physics/ is CC BY 4.0; the page footer also prints a noncommercial clause, so this card does not copy the sentence. Supports the sentence that drag opposes motion through a fluid, and that air resistance is a form of friction.
